entities.name: Bacurius I of Iberia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bacurius I of Iberia was a king (mepe) of the Arsacid dynasty, ruling from 234 to 249 CE.

As the ruler of Iberia, he played a crucial role in the region's politics and economy during the Late Antiquity period. His reign saw significant cultural and religious developments, including the spread of Christianity and the rise of the Church of Iberia.

Bacurius I's legacy extends beyond his own kingdom, as he contributed to the broader historical context of the Roman Empire's decline and the emergence of new powers in the region.

In the annals of history, Bacurius I stands as a testament to the complexities of state-building and the resilience of ancient civilizations in the face of shifting global forces.

The longevity of Christianity in the region, facilitated by the patronage of Bacurius I, would have profound repercussions on the development of Eastern Orthodoxy.
